subject: Subprocessor transparency & vendor hardening matrix — follow-up
messages:
From: Anya Novak <anya.novak@cobaltinsurance.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@cobaltinsurance.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Subprocessor detail request for RFP — list + notification policies

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the quick demo earlier this week. As part of our RFP packet we need a clear inventory of Redwood's subprocessors and the assurances you provide for critical cloud and telemetry vendors. Specifically we need:

- a vendor list (name, role, country) called out by category (cloud infra, observability, analytics, backups)
- whether each subprocessor stores customer data (yes/no) and the types of data stored
- evidence or links to attestations (SOC 2 report, ISO certs, AUP links)
- your policy for notifying customers of subprocessor changes (how much notice, channels used) and a sample change notice

We are on a tight procurement cadence; would appreciate the matrix and any supporting artifacts by EOD next Wednesday (Feb 25). Also flag any subprocessors that are non-US or have cross-border transfers.

Best,
Anya Novak
Senior Sourcing Manager — Cobalt Insurance
anya.novak@cobaltinsurance.com

P.S. We have a standard security questionnaire that we may send after we review the vendor matrix.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anya Novak <anya.novak@cobaltinsurance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor detail request for RFP — list + notification policies

Hi Anya —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a preliminary subprocessor matrix (redwood_subprocessor_matrix_2026-02.csv) and our Security Pack (security_pack_v3.pdf) that contains SOC 2 Type II dates, summary of controls, and our Data Processing Addendum. Highlights below:

- Cloud infra: AWS (us-west-2 primary, eu-west-1 DR). AWS stores temporary inference request data for routing and autoscaling; persistent customer data is only in customer-controlled storage when explicitly configured.
- Metrics & Logging: Datadog (US-only account for hosted), Sentry (error telemetry; sampling for PII avoidance). Logs are retained per customer config in the Console; default retention is 30 days.
- Analytics & Usage: Segment (event ingestion), BigQuery (analytics warehouse) — these are used for product analytics and are configured with least privilege roles; we can restrict exports for regulated customers.
- Backups & Storage: Google Cloud Storage used for non-production artifacts; snapshots encrypted with customer keys where requested.

Notification policy:
- For low-impact vendor changes (minor version upgrades, patching) we send a quarterly bulletin.
- For material changes (new subprocessor, change in data export/import behaviour, location change) we commit to 30 calendar days' notice via email to the primary security contact and an in-console alert.
- For emergency security patches where waiting 30 days would be unsafe, we notify within 24 hours after remediation with details and mitigation steps.

We include links to our latest SOC 2 summary and a vetted subprocessor agreement in the Security Pack. If you need a signed Data Processing Addendum or KMS-HSM-usage attestation, Marissa can expedite.

Attaching the CSV and PDF now. Let me know if you want a redacted sample of a change notice template.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_2026-02.csv (CSV, 48KB), security_pack_v3.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB)

From: Anya Novak <anya.novak@cobaltinsurance.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor detail request for RFP — list + notification policies

Rishi —

Thanks for that. A couple quick clarifications after scanning the CSV:

1) KMS / key custody: your matrix notes that customer-managed keys are available for dedicated/private deployments. For hosted customers, do you support AWS KMS CMKs per-customer, or is it a platform-managed key? We need the exact modes supported and whether the key material ever leaves AWS KMS.

2) Data residency: you indicated GCS for non-production snapshots. Do you offer region-locking for EU-only processing for EU-regulated customers? If so, what region choices and what controls ensure no cross-border backups?

3) Change notice: 30 days is acceptable. Could you send a sample of your "material change" notice language and the in-console banner mockup you referenced? Procurement will attach the notice as an SLA exhibit.

If you can answer 1–3 and share the change-notice sample by Friday EOD (Feb 27), we can keep to procurement timelines.

Appreciate it —
Anya

On a separate note, our Security team will likely ping Marissa directly for the SOC 2 artifacts next week.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anya Novak <anya.novak@cobaltinsurance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor detail request for RFP — list + notification policies

Anya / procurement team —

Quick follow-up with exactly what you asked for:

1) KMS / key custody (hosted):
- Hosted (SaaS): platform-managed KMS is the default (AWS KMS CMKs). Customer key material never leaves AWS KMS; we use AWS KMS for envelope encryption and limit key access via IAM roles. For customers requiring customer-managed keys in hosted mode, we offer a dedicated customer CMK option (charges apply) where the CMK is provisioned in a customer-dedicated AWS account and access is brokered via cross-account IAM roles. Details in security_pack_v3.pdf (see section 3.2).

2) Data residency / region-locking:
- We support region-restricted hosting for Enterprise contracts: US (us-west-2), EU (eu-west-1), APAC (ap-southeast-1). For EU-only customers we put inference runtime, KV cache, and analytics in the eu-west-1 partition and disable cross-region backups by default; this is enforced by our deployment policy and audited during onboarding. Non-production snapshot copies are by default restricted to the same region, and any cross-region snapshoting requires explicit written approval in the contract.

3) Material change notice (sample):
- Subject: Important: Redwood Inference planned subprocessor addition (Databricks) — action required
- Body (summary): We are writing to inform you that Redwood Inference plans to add Databricks (US) as an analytics subprocessor to support increased analytics throughput. Expected date: 2026-03-25. Data types involved: aggregated usage metrics (no raw inference content). Reason: performance/scalability. Impact: none to customer-configured persistence; default logging sampling unaffected. Your options: opt-out via configuration request within 30 days (instructions included). If you require, we will provide a side-letter to prohibit use for your account.

In-console banner mockup: [IN-CONSOLE: Banner displayed 30 days prior, links to notice, and a one-click "Request exclusion" button]. I can export a PNG mockup if you want.

Marissa — can you please prepare the SOC 2 Type II cover letter and the DPA signature page for Cobalt? Chloe — please add a redlined exhibit clause for the change-notice SLA language and attach the sample notice as an exhibit. I'm looping you both so we can turn these around quickly.

Anya — attaching the change-notice sample as plain text and a brief PNG mockup link in the Security Pack. If Cobalt needs an on-record commitment around the side-letter opt-out, we can scope that into the enterprise deal.

Thanks,
Rishi
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
